contribute.title: Contribute
contribute.lead: Write a lesson, suggest a free work, correct a mistake or share an idea. No account needed. Everything is read by the curators before it enters the collection.
contribute.description: Send a lesson, suggest a free work or correct a mistake. Every contribution is reviewed.
rules: Write in your own words. Do not copy texts protected by copyright.
Every lesson needs at least one reliable source.
Do not send files or links to pirated copies: the library only points to legitimate sources.
Published lessons are released under the CC BY-SA 4.0 licence.
steps: Fill in the form below. The draft is saved in this browser while you write.
Volunteers check the sources, the text and the licence.
Once approved, the contribution is published under the name you give.
Every version is recorded. If something goes wrong, we just go back to the previous one.

dedication.title: For Lúcia
dedication.etym: From Latin Lucia, feminine of Lucius, derived from lux, lucis: “light”.
senses: The luminous one; she who brings light.
According to tradition, a name given in ancient Rome to children born at dawn.
In this project: the grandmother to whom this library is dedicated.
dedication.related: From the same root: lucid, elucidate, illuminate.
text: This project bears the name of Lúcia, the grandmother of the person who created it.
She is no longer here, but the name remained, and with it what such a name promises: light.
Every library is a way of turning on the light for someone. May everyone who learns something here carry a little of that brightness forward.

support.title: Support Instituto Lúcia
support.lead: The library is free and has no ads, and it will stay that way, with or without your contribution.
paragraphs: Instituto Lúcia has no sponsor, sells no courses and does not sell your data. It is kept going by volunteer work, because knowledge is not a commodity.

Even so, keeping a site online costs money. Those who can help pay that bill guarantee access for those who cannot. That is how the working class has always built what is its own: by pooling the little each one has.
The money raised has a clear destination:
costs: Domain and hosting for the site.
Storage for audio and for backup copies of the collection.
Whatever is left goes into expanding the collection: more lessons, more translations, more reviewing.
support.optional: Donating is entirely optional. Nobody loses access to anything for not contributing, and there is no exclusive content for donors. If money is tight, do not donate: study, share a lesson or come and volunteer. That sustains the project too.
support.note: Contributions are made on Benfeitoria, a Brazilian crowdfunding platform. This site neither receives nor stores payment data.
support.wallLead: Those who helped keep the institute standing and chose to leave their name here.

community.title: Conversations
community.lead: Ask questions, propose study groups and help those who are starting out. The institute's focus is teaching; this space exists to support study.
rules: Respect always: disagree with ideas, do not attack people.
No racism, sexism, LGBT-phobia, ableism or any hate speech.
Do not post personal data, yours or anyone else's.
Stating a fact? Give the source.
